metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Fairchance, Fayette County? We buy Marcellus and legacy gas interests near Uniontown and the old furnace district. No pressure to sell.
heroLead: Fairchance grew up around an iron furnace, not a gas well, but the coke-and-iron-era deeds still shape how mineral rights get sorted out here today.
intro: Fairchance sits just south of Uniontown, named for the old Fairchance Furnace that once smelted iron using local ore and coke. Land in and around the borough carries that industrial history in its deed records, with mineral rights sometimes split off from the surface decades before anyone thought about natural gas.

We buy mineral and royalty interests near Fairchance, whether your family's acreage is producing under a Marcellus lease, sitting idle under an older agreement, or split among several heirs who inherited a share of the same parcel.

sections.heading: Fayette County's flank position in the Marcellus play
paragraphs: Fairchance sits toward the southern edge of Fayette County's Marcellus activity, which is generally lighter than the wet-gas core in Washington and Greene counties to the west. Some nearby tracts have seen horizontal development; others remain leased with no drilling yet, which is a normal state for this part of the county.

sections.heading: Furnace-era deeds and what they mean now
paragraphs: Because Fairchance's economy was built on iron and coke rather than coal alone, some of the oldest severance deeds here separated mineral rights in ways that don't always match what neighboring coal-patch towns did. We read the actual recorded language rather than assuming a standard pattern applies.
We've reviewed enough of these older Fayette County instruments to know that assumptions rarely hold up, so we read the actual recorded language every time.

sections.heading: What we'll want to see
paragraphs: A lease, division order, or royalty statement helps, but even a parcel description is enough for us to start pulling records through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds in Uniontown.

faqs.question: Is there active Marcellus drilling near Fairchance?
faqs.answer: Development in this part of Fayette County is lighter than the core wet-gas counties further west, and activity varies tract to tract, so we look at what's actually happening near your specific parcel.

faqs.question: My deed mentions an old furnace company. Does that affect my oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: It might, depending on how mineral rights were severed historically in that transaction. We review the actual recorded deed language before assuming anything about what you currently own.

faqs.question: Can you buy my share if I only inherited part of the mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, fractional interests inherited from family land near Fairchance are common, and we regularly buy a single heir's share.

faqs.question: Does the old Fairchance Furnace history ever show up in modern deed disputes?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, when boundary descriptions from that era are vague by today's survey standards, but it rarely affects who holds the oil and gas rights themselves — it's more often a surface boundary question than a mineral ownership one.
